text:
ryan: heads up — ran an nsys capture on the long-tailed latency batch yesterday. timeline looks weird: host->device memcpy shows up earlier but the big gpt_attention_fwd kernel doesn't start for ~12ms after. also see KV prefetch kernels interleaved across streams. is this a CUDA stream submission delay or CPU scheduling gap? :thinking:
linh: can you paste the timeline screenshot or the exported csv? quick guess: either the hostcopy thread got preempted, or there's a serialized syscall between submits.
ryan: attaching snippet from nsys: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none -o run1 ./server --trace-run` and export -> timeline. here's two rows (rough):
  hostMemcpyH2D_stream2  0.004ms - 0.008ms
  gpt_attention_fwd      12.340ms - 15.120ms
  kv_prefetch_stream1    7.100ms - 7.400ms
kevin: that gap is suspicious. do we have pinned allocations for those prefetched buffers? if host memory is pageable, cudaMemcpyAsync may block and cause scheduling weirdness. also check if batcher thread is doing a join/lock around submit.
maya: i re-ran with `--alloc-pinned` and bumping the hostcopy thread to SCHED_RR in our test harness. median p50 dropped 4ms, the weird gap disappeared in the timeline. results: original p90 42ms -> pinned+rt p90 38ms.
ryan: nice. so pinned memory helps but doesn't explain why the kernel was queued much later than memcpy. could be kernel selection path in runtime adds work on CPU before enqueue. maybe quantization fallback path triggers extra CPU work for some batches.
linh: good call — i grep'd logs: `kernel_select: chosen=k_f32_attention alt=k_int8_attention reason=fallback_missing_kernels` for some batches. if we fall back to f32 kernels we do extra workspace alloc + memcpy staging on CPU before launch. that would add serialization.
kevin: aha — mixed problem: (1) pageable host copy + CPU preempt -> memcpy shows earlier but not actually committed to GPU until later, (2) kernel selection fallback does CPU work before launch. combined produce the long idle.
ryan: what about stream priorities? maybe prefetch stream is high priority but attention kernels are launched on default stream so they wait. should we try assigning kernels to per-ctx priority streams?
maya: i tried a quick patch to use `cudaStreamCreateWithPriority` for the run queue (prio higher than prefetch). timeline showed attention kernels preempting prefetch and overall p95 dropped 6%. caveat: increased contention on GPU for small kernels.
linh: for reproducible capture, run nsys with `--sample=cpu` and also capture `nvtxRangePush` around kernel_select path to correlate CPU stacks. i can add a small NVTX span in the selection hot path.
kevin: also add `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` for unified allocations; that made H2D latency more deterministic in my tests.
ryan: action items: (1) add NVTX around kernel selection (linh), (2) switch to pinned allocations by default for prefetch buffer (maya), (3) make batcher avoid heavyweight selection on hot path — cache kernel choice per model/seq-length (kevin), (4) re-run nsys with stream priorities toggled and attach timelines (ryan).
infra-bot: CI job #4821: nsys-run-2091234567 triggered by ryan. link: https://ci.redwood/4821/logs (capturing full trace).
maya: re-run w/ pinned+nvtx+priority — quick numbers: baseline mean=28.3ms, pinned+prio mean=24.9ms, pinned+prio+kernel-cache mean=21.7ms. will open a small PR with kernel cache micro-optimizations.
linh: once PR lands i'll pick up NVTX spans and run full perfetto export. can someone confirm we want kernel_cache keyed by (model_id, seq_len, dtype_profile)?
kevin: yes, that key looks right. also record fallback reasons so we can detect drifting kernel availability on rollout. add a metric: fallback_rate per 1000 requests.
ryan: great. thanks all. i'll triage follow-ups into the runtime perf board. if anyone sees another timeline with similar gap, drop it here. :thumbsup:
